senses.sense_definition: A sudden and unexpected large amount of money or other benefit.

examples.text: The unexpected inheritance was a massive <w>windfall</w> for the struggling family.
The company used the tax <w>windfall</w> to invest in new technology and staff.

senses.sense_definition: A fruit that has fallen from a tree naturally due to wind.

examples.text: We gathered the <w>windfall</w> apples from the orchard floor to make cider.
The ground was covered in <w>windfall</w> pears after the heavy storm last night.

senses.sense_definition: Something, such as a tree or branch, that has been blown down by the wind.

examples.text: The forest path was blocked by a large <w>windfall</w> after the hurricane.
Clearing the <w>windfall</w> from the driveway took the entire afternoon.

senses.sense_definition: The process or event of trees being blown down by strong winds.

examples.text: The forest management plan aims to reduce the risk of <w>windfall</w> in older stands.
Severe <w>windfall</w> occurred across the valley during the winter storms.
